title: Day 1 — Arrival 🛬
description: Fly in, check in to Il Monastero Collection. Drop the bags, breathe the air, find food. The trip begins.
fun_fact: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country — 58. You're about to see some of the best of them.

title: Day 2 — Il Monastero 🕌
description: A slower day based at Il Monastero. Walk the surrounding countryside. Find the best local restaurant and stay too long.
fun_fact: Umbria is called the green heart of Italy — the only landlocked region in central Italy. Medieval hilltowns, truffles, and very few tourists.

title: Day 3 — Assisi 🙏
description: Check in to Hotel Assisi. Walk up to the Basilica di San Francesco — one of the most beautiful churches in Italy. The town is tiny; you can walk everything in an afternoon.
fun_fact: St Francis gave up wealth and a military career after a series of visions in his early twenties. He founded an order of 5,000 friars before dying at 44. The Basilica began construction within two years of his death.

title: Day 4 — Fattoria Fibbiano 🍷
description: Drive west into Tuscany. Hotel Fattoria Fibbiano is a working winery in the Pisan hills — vineyards, olive groves, terracotta. Wine tasting this evening is not optional.
fun_fact: Tuscany has 11 DOCG wine designations — the highest Italian quality tier. The Pisan hills produce wines most tourists never encounter because they barely leave the region.

title: Day 5 — Tuscan Hills 🌻
description: Still at Fattoria Fibbiano. Drive into Volterra — an Etruscan city so old it predates Rome, perched dramatically on a cliff above the Tuscan valleys.
fun_fact: Volterra was a major Etruscan city when Rome was still a village. They built here around 800 BC, and their civilisation gave Rome its alphabet, arch construction, and religious practices.

title: Day 6 — Hotel Recostano 🌿
description: Check in to Hotel Recostano Residence. The last stop before home. Find the best local restaurant and eat slowly.
fun_fact: The word Tuscany comes from the Etruscan people (Tusci in Latin) who dominated central Italy before Rome. Even the name of the land still remembers them.

title: Day 7 — Last Night 🌅
description: The last full day. No rushing. Buy good olive oil and a bottle of something excellent. Walk somewhere beautiful. Eat a long dinner. Come back to the room slow. Early start tomorrow.
fun_fact: Italy is the world's largest wine producer. The average Italian drinks about 40 litres per year. They consider this moderate.

title: Day 8 — Fly Home ✈️
description: Flight W4 6245 at 05:55 — early alarm. On the plane, close your eyes and go through every meal, every piazza, every evening. You'll be back.
fun_fact: Norway and Italy are both long and narrow countries running roughly north–south. Norway has the fjords, Italy has the shape of a boot. Both are convinced theirs is the most beautiful country in the world.
